trust_model: Compact imports require independent recent height/block/state anchor and separately pinned genesis/committee schedule. Peer-advertised hashes are not authority. Local authorized checkpoint metadata and minimum-anchor marker are trusted on restart. Whole-store privileged rollback is outside the threat model.
environment: Debian 13 managed two-core host. Native ALSA/libudev development files supplied outside repository for desktop regressions. Docker internal/none networks, two-CPU/two-GiB limits; host filesystem is smaller than 20 GB and Docker uses copied container roots.
limits: Signing reservations and unresolved evidence are retained indefinitely; eventual safe quota refusal remains.
Active state snapshot cap is 100000 nonce/name entries and 16 MiB; full checkpoint cap 17 MiB.
Directory pressure scans grow with retained file counts; benchmark scaling is not million-entry validation.
Hard filesystem quota provisioning is required for absolute allocation bounds including concurrent WAL/external export writes and filesystem overhead.
Fresh recent checkpoint anchors require an independently authenticated operator channel; no automatic trust-anchor selection or snapshot network-download protocol is implemented.
No public deployment, real staking, issuance or payments; all production YPP versions remain rejected.
development_findings: Initial process harness compared normal per-height WAL contents across live height advancement; corrected to retain exact WAL checks only during offline maintenance, with immutable signing/evidence checks across live restarts.
The reserve guard safely stopped a P2P run when copied Docker roots consumed build-disk headroom; rebuildable debug artifacts were cleaned, then final runs passed.

A finite forged discovery burst delayed one endpoint update under the old four-datagram receive budget. Final code cheaply drains at most 64 datagrams while retaining the four-page signature budget; final adversarial campaign passed.
